name: Sterilise
summary: Clean first, then kill what’s left: dirt shields germs from heat, chlorine and light. Boiling handles most needs, and a pressure cooker at full pressure reaches the temperature hospitals sterilise at. Diluted bleach or pool chlorine disinfects surfaces and tools. UV-C lamps hide in pond clarifiers, air purifiers and water treatment units, but they burn eyes and skin.

parts.why: Bleach and pool chlorine disinfect surfaces and tools
UV-C lamps kill germs on surfaces and in water
Electric boiling and steaming where power allows
Fuel for boiling and pressure cooking

tips: Boil tools for 10 minutes. A pressure cooker at full pressure for 15–30 minutes sterilises.
Never mix bleach with ammonia, vinegar or other cleaners. It makes toxic gas.
Never look at a lit UV-C lamp, and keep skin out of its light.
Bleach loses strength over months. Old bottles need a stronger mix.
